To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we designed a near-infrared fluorescent hybrid nanocomposite with multiple Au clusters in an apo H-fertin nanocage for kidney specific bioimaging.

we designed a new near-infrared (800-900 nm) fluorescence probe based on gold cluster and apo H-ferritins, and the probe showed strong fluorescence efficiency, powerful tissue penetrating ability and kidney-targeted specificity in vivo.

we designed and synthesized the first native protein guided Au cluster-based nanocomposite with near-infrared fluorescence, which showed strong tissue-penetrating ability, strong fluorescent emission efficiency and excellent kidney targeting properties.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design, synthesis and application of Au cluster-based hybrid nanomaterials.
the synthesis of a novel near-infrared fluorescent nanoprobe based on multiple gold clusters within an apo ferritin nanocage.

the development of novel nanomaterials and their applications in biomedicine and nanomedicine, including the design and synthesis of multifunctional nanomaterials, the study of the interactions of nanoparticles with biological systems, and the development of nanomaterials-based biosensors, bioimaging probes and theranostics.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the fine-tuning of HFt nanocage with the assembly of multiple Au clusters has led to a NIR Au-HFtnanocomposite, with enhanced fluorescence quantum yield and kidney-specific targeting capability, for NIR biowindow imaging and theranosis of kidney diseases.
the design of NIR Au-HFts is a promising strategy for kidney specific imaging and theranosis.
the Au-HFt nanocages have great potential for biomedical applications, especially for NIR imaging and theranosis of kidney disease.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have successfully integrated a near-infrared fluorescent Au cluster-based nanocomposite into a native protein-guided nanostructure, which has shown powerful tissue penetrating ability and strong fluorescent efficiency, as well as excellent kidney targeting specificity.

we have designed a new type of nanomaterials, the NIR Au-HFts, which have the advantages of both the protein and the Au cluster, for the first time, and have shown their great promise as kidney-specific targeting nanoprobes for in vivo imaging.
the Au-HFt nanocomposites with a defined structure, composition and function can be designed and constructed through molecular simulation and molecular engineering.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we can design and synthesize a series of novel hybrid nanocomposites by integrating the functionality of biological molecules with novel physiochemical and functional properties of the metal cluster.
the design of a hybrid nanocomposite with multiple Au clusters inside a HFt nanocage is a promising approach for NIR fluorescent kidney targeting imaging.
the design and synthesis of protein-guided nanomaterials with defined molecular level structures is a promising strategy to develop novel nanomaterials that can be used for in vivo bioimaging.
